chapter: Image, travel and Black, Brown and Beige
title: White swing bands versus the 'soul brothers'
summary: Greer says white bands were good collectively but not on solos, and Black musicians had to be twice as good.

bands.name: Les Brown and His Band of Renown

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, what did you think about -- how did you like the white bands that were around at the time, did you think of Benny Goodman, Artie Shaw. What/ those guys?
You told me already about how you all slaughtered Goodman in Chicago---Fats Waller sat in with you all.

They were good. I like Tommy, I liked Tommy's band, I liked Glen Miller's band. And Woody had a good band. And what's the guy played with Bob Hope? Les Brown and his Band of Renown, I liked him. We played against him when he was still in school. I like them bands, they were good.

Collectively they were nice, but when you come to individual solos they didn't stack up to the soul brothers. Soul brothers would eat 'em up. Because they didn't think like we did. You see, rhythm is your heritage. That's us. And dancing, singing is our heritage.
But, you know, they didn't believe it. You'd have to put it in front of the eyes and they still didn't believe it. You know what I mean. Burn 'em down.

And we had to be -- you know, it was necessary. We had to be twice as good as them guys, you know. Now you do--- for recognition. You had to be twice as good. Had to be twice as good singing, twice as good dancing, playing the music. It goes to show you. They say no greater compliment in the world than to be imitated, you know. They're all imitating. All of them want to be soul, soul brothers. That's a big joke. If you ain't got no soul you sure ain't going to be down here with your soul gone, you ain't going to be sitting up here playing music. So that's stupid.
But like I tell you, man, Buster Bailey, Bushell -- you remember Garvin Bushell?

MR. GREER: He played all the lead instruments. But you think he's sitting with the philharmonic orchestra? No, because he's soul. But he was capable. I ain't seen the day, even the day that Benny Goodman could play like Buster Bailey. Buster ate him up like a turkey dinner. And Jimmy Hamilton, Barney. So, they splice him, the King of Swing. They'd carry him down. He playing the same thing out of Fletcher's book, years ago. Fletcher saved him. But right away they're going to make him the white champion.
